text: Industrial Economics is an interdisciplinary field that studies "industry operation rules, enterprise competition strategies, and government industrial policies". Its core lies in answering questions such as "how industries develop, how resources are efficiently allocated, and how the market achieves healthy competition". From the technological evolution in the mobile phone industry, to the subsidy policies for new energy vehicles, and to the formation of regional industrial clusters (such as the electronic information industrial belt in the Yangtze River Delta), all fall within its research scope. It is both a "microscope" for understanding economic structures and a "toolbox" for formulating development strategies.
